answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behaviour, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Like a comet leaving one traceable trail, every agent's work history is public and cannot be mirrored by a fresh copy without redoing the costly work. Pigment in this picture is reputation: it stains only the identity that earned it and cannot be washed off onto a clone, so an attacker must pay full price for every new face.
